sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache connecting ridge
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ("Connecting Ridge") (2022 list; not among NASA's nine 2024 regions)
sites.description: Raised ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; one of the best-lit spots near the pole.
sites.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030, as tabulated in Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, 170-178, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2017.07.006 (Table 1: 89.45°S, 222.69°E); also Site 1 of Gläser et al. 2014, Icarus 243. Inside NASA's Artemis III 'Connecting Ridge' candidate region (2022)

sites.name: Shackleton crater rim
sites.mission: Long-studied rim point; Artemis region 'Peak near Shackleton' (2022 list; not among NASA's nine 2024 regions)
sites.description: Rim of the 21 km crater at the pole. High sun incidence, but the crater's own walls shape the horizon.
sites.source: Bussey et al. 2010, Icarus 208, 558-564, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.03.028 (Point A, rim of Shackleton crater: 89.68°S, 166.0°W)

sites.name: Shackleton crater floor (PSR)
sites.mission: Permanently shadowed region (PSR): cold trap for volatiles
sites.description: Crater floor ~4 km below the rim. The Sun never clears the walls, a control case for 'permanent shadow'.
sites.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature: Shackleton crater centre 89.67°S 129.78°E

sites.name: de Gerlache crater rim
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('de Gerlache Rim')
sites.description: Rim of the 32 km de Gerlache crater, about 50 km from Shackleton.
sites.source: Bussey et al. 2010, Icarus 208, 558-564, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.03.028 (Point C, rim of de Gerlache crater: 88.71°S, 68.7°W)

sites.name: Malapert massif
sites.description: NASA's notional Artemis III landing site on Mons Malapert, a 5 km high massif on the Earth-facing side; it trades some sunlight for an excellent view of Earth.
sites.source: Kring et al. 2025, 'Notional Geological Traverses, Station Activities, and Sample Collection on Mons Malapert, Lunar South Polar Region', JGR Planets 130, e2024JE008905, doi:10.1029/2024JE008905 (NASA notional landing site: 85.964°S, 357.681°E)

sites.name: Mons Mouton (IM-2 Athena)
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Mons Mouton', 2024); Intuitive Machines IM-2 'Athena' landed here in March 2025
sites.description: Flat-topped plateau ~160 km from the pole. Athena landed nearby and ended early after tipping over.
sites.source: LROC team, 'IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely' (lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1408): Athena at rest at 84.7906°S, 29.1957°E

sites.name: Nobile crater western rim
sites.mission: Former VIPER rover target; Artemis III candidate ('Nobile Rim')
sites.description: Western rim of Nobile crater, chosen for rover traverses between lit ridges and shadowed pockets.
sites.source: Beyer et al. 2025, 'VIPER Site Analysis', Planetary Science Journal 6, 236, doi:10.3847/PSJ/ae061a (centre of the VIPER primary mission area: 85.42088°S, 31.6218°E)

sites.name: Haworth crater north rim
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Haworth', 2024), on the rim above the permanently shadowed crater
sites.description: Crest of Haworth crater's north rim, above the permanently shadowed floor, facing the Earth-side meridian.
sites.source: Rim crest derived by the team from NASA LRO LOLA polar topography (148 m grid): highest point on Haworth's rim where the ground falls at least 150 m on both sides, searched 20-32 km from the IAU crater centre (87.45 S, 5.0 W). Haworth is one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (release 24-136, 28 Oct 2024); NASA publishes no point.

sites.name: Faustini crater rim
sites.mission: Artemis III candidate region ('Faustini Rim A') (2022 list; not among NASA's nine 2024 regions)
sites.description: Candidate landing site FRA02 on the rim of the permanently shadowed Faustini crater: of the Faustini Rim A sites with published coordinates, it has the longest unbroken sunlit stretches in the midsummers of 2025 to 2032.
sites.source: Wueller et al. 2026, 'Assessing Potential Landing Sites With Favorable Illumination and Accessible, Potentially Volatile-Rich Permanently Shadowed Regions Within Artemis Candidate Landing Regions', JGR Planets 131, e2025JE009434, doi:10.1029/2025JE009434 (Table A1, site FRA02: 87.7490°S, 95.0840°E)

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram / Shiv Shakti point)
sites.description: High southern latitude but not polar: ordinary day/night cycle with a low Sun.
sites.source: ISRO; LROC NAC image release (Aug 2023): 69.373°S 32.319°E

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.description: Equatorial near side: a 14-day day and 14-day night, with Earth fixed high in the sky.
sites.source: LROC / Davies & Colvin 2000 (0.67408°N, 23.47297°E)

sites.name: Chang'e-4 (Von Kármán crater)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-4, first far-side landing, Jan 2019
sites.description: Far side: Earth never rises. All communications go through a relay satellite (Queqiao).
sites.source: Liu et al. 2019, Nature Communications 10:4229 (45.4446°S 177.5991°E)

sites.name: Apollo 12 (Ocean of Storms)
sites.description: Near-equatorial mare site next to Surveyor 3: a two-week day and a two-week night, with Earth high in the sky.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 3.01239°S 23.42157°W

sites.name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
sites.description: Fra Mauro highlands: ordinary equatorial lighting with Earth high overhead.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 3.64530°S 17.47136°W

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley–Apennine)
sites.description: Beside Hadley Rille under the Apennine mountains: local relief rises a few degrees, so sunrise and sunset shift slightly.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 26.13222°N 3.63386°E

sites.name: Apollo 16 (Descartes highlands)
sites.description: Central highlands: equatorial lighting with Earth high in the sky.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 8.97301°S 15.50019°E

sites.name: Apollo 17 (Taurus–Littrow)
sites.description: A valley between massifs on the edge of Mare Serenitatis: steep surrounding terrain delays sunrise and hastens sunset.
sites.source: Davies & Colvin 2000, JGR 105(E8):20277 (Apollo landing-site coordinates in the lunar mean-Earth frame): 20.19080°N 30.77168°E

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-1, NASA CLPS, February 2024
sites.description: The southernmost landing before IM-2: a low Sun and Earth low over the northern horizon.
sites.source: LROC NAC post-landing image release (Feb 2024): ~80.13°S 1.44°E

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mons Latreille, Mare Crisium)
sites.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1, NASA CLPS, March 2025
sites.description: Near-side mare near the eastern limb: Earth sits low in the western sky.
sites.source: Firefly / LROC release (Mar 2025): ~18.56°N 61.81°E

sites.name: IM-3 target (Reiner Gamma swirl)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-3, NASA CLPS, planned
sites.description: A lunar swirl with a local magnetic field on the western near side; target area, not a landing point.
sites.source: NASA CLPS task order announcement: Reiner Gamma region (approximate centre)

sites.name: Chang'e-3 (Mare Imbrium)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-3 with the Yutu rover, December 2013
sites.description: Northern mare plain: Earth in the southern sky for the whole lunar day.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~44.12°N 19.51°W

sites.name: Chang'e-5 (Mons Rümker area)
sites.description: Young mare basalts in Oceanus Procellarum: the most recent sample-return site before Chang'e-6.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~43.06°N 51.92°W

sites.name: Chang'e-6 (Apollo basin, far side)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-6, first far-side sample return, June 2024
sites.description: Far side: Earth never rises, so all communication goes through the Queqiao-2 relay.
sites.source: Published post-landing position (CNSA / LROC): ~41.64°S 153.99°W

sites.name: SLIM (near Shioli crater)
sites.description: Near-side highlands: equatorial lighting; the lander came to rest tilted, so its panels faced west.
sites.source: JAXA post-landing position: ~13.316°S 25.251°E

sites.name: Luna 24 (Mare Crisium)
sites.description: Eastern near-side mare: Earth low in the western sky.
sites.source: LROC identification of the Luna 24 lander: ~12.71°N 62.21°E

sites.name: Luna 25 target (Boguslawsky crater)
sites.mission: Roscosmos Luna 25 planned landing site; the spacecraft crashed in August 2023
sites.description: High southern latitude near Boguslawsky crater: a low Sun and Earth low in the north.
sites.source: Roscosmos / IKI pre-launch landing ellipse centre: ~69.55°S 43.54°E

sites.name: Griffin Mission One target (Nobile region)
sites.mission: Astrobotic Griffin Mission One, NASA CLPS (CP-10), planned no earlier than early 2027 on Falcon Heavy
sites.description: South polar target near Mons Mouton, west of Nobile crater (VIPER's original area). Carries Astrolab's FLIP rover. Target region; the exact point is not published.
sites.source: Astrobotic Griffin-1 mission updates; Wikipedia "Griffin Mission One" (Nobile region near Mons Mouton)

sites.name: IM-4 target (Mons Mouton)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-4, NASA CLPS, planned 2027
sites.description: South polar plateau of Mons Mouton. Target region; shown at IM-2 Athena's landing area because IM-4's exact point is not published.
sites.source: NASA CLPS deliveries / Intuitive Machines (Mons Mouton target)

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 2 target (near Nassau crater, far side)
sites.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 2, NASA CLPS, far side, planned 2026-2027 (with the LuSEE-Night radio telescope)
sites.description: Far-side site near Nassau crater, shielded from Earth radio noise; Earth is never in view, so data are relayed by the Elytra orbiter. Approximate crater centre.
sites.source: Firefly Aerospace "Blue Ghost Mission 2" page (near Nassau Crater); Wikipedia "Blue Ghost Mission 2"

sites.name: APEX 1.0 target (Schrödinger basin)
sites.mission: Draper / ispace-U.S. APEX 1.0, NASA CLPS (CP-12), Schrödinger basin, planned
sites.description: Far-side impact basin near the south pole. Shown at the basin centre; the landing point is not published.
sites.source: NASA CLPS deliveries (Schrödinger basin); IAU gazetteer basin centre

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 3 target (Gruithuisen Domes)
sites.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 3, NASA CLPS, Gruithuisen Domes, planned 2028
sites.description: Silica-rich volcanic domes on the northwest near side. Approximate dome location.
sites.source: NASA CLPS deliveries (Gruithuisen Domes); approximate position of Gruithuisen Gamma

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 4 target (Haworth crater rim)
sites.mission: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 4, NASA CLPS (CS-6), south pole, planned 2029
sites.description: Rim of Haworth crater near the south pole. The exact point is not published, so the analysis point is the north rim crest, 31 km from the crater centre (found from the LOLA 40 m elevation profile).
sites.source: NASA CLPS award announcement (July 2025): rim of Haworth crater

sites.name: IM-5 target (Mons Malapert)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-5, NASA CLPS, Mons Malapert, planned around 2030
sites.description: Malapert massif ridge near the south pole, also an Artemis III candidate region. Shown at the Malapert site's coordinates.
sites.source: Intuitive Machines CLPS award release (2026): Mons Malapert

sites.name: Blue Moon MK1 Pathfinder target (near Shackleton)
sites.mission: Blue Origin Blue Moon MK1 Pathfinder (carries NASA CLPS payload SCALPSS), planned early 2027
sites.description: Demonstration landing near Shackleton crater. Shown at the Shackleton rim site; the exact point is not published.
sites.source: Wikipedia "Blue Moon Pathfinder Mission 1" (south pole, near Shackleton crater)

sites.name: Chang'e-7 target (Shackleton southeast ridge)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-7, south pole, launch postponed from August 2026 to 2027
sites.description: Peak on the southeast ridge of Shackleton crater, to search for water ice.
sites.source: Reported landing site 88.8°S, 123.4°E (A. Jones, 2023); CNN, Aug 2026 (postponed)

sites.name: Chang'e-8 target (Leibnitz Beta / Mons Mouton)
sites.mission: CNSA Chang'e-8, south pole, planned around 2028
sites.description: Reported to focus on the Leibnitz Beta plateau (Mons Mouton). Shown at the Mons Mouton site; candidate region only.
sites.source: Media reports (2025) on Chang'e-8 site selection; Wikipedia "Chang'e 8"

sites.name: Chandrayaan-4 target (Mons Mouton, MM-4)
sites.mission: ISRO Chandrayaan-4 sample return, south pole, planned 2028
sites.description: Reported site MM-4 in the Mons Mouton region (not yet confirmed by ISRO). Shown at the Mons Mouton site.
sites.source: News reports (2026) of ISRO selecting site MM-4 near Mons Mouton; Space.com (2028 target)

sites.name: Luna 27 target zone
sites.mission: Roscosmos Luna 27, south polar region, planned 2028 or later
sites.description: Centre of the published landing zone (79°S to 83°S, 1°W to 51°E); a zone, not a point.
sites.source: Landing site choice for Luna-27 (Acta Astronautica, 2024)

sites.name: Luna 2 impact (Palus Putredinis)
sites.description: First spacecraft to reach the Moon: a planned impact east of Mare Imbrium.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1959-014A|title: 29.1°N 0.0°E

sites.name: Ranger 4 crash (far side)
sites.description: First US craft to reach the Moon; a dead computer meant it hit the far side without returning data.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1962-012A|title: 15.5°S 130.7°W

sites.name: Ranger 6 impact (Mare Tranquillitatis)
sites.description: Hit on target in Mare Tranquillitatis, but its cameras failed and no images came back.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1964-007A|title: 9.358°N 21.48°E

sites.name: Ranger 7 impact (Mare Cognitum)
sites.description: First close-up US images of the Moon, sent back until impact in Mare Cognitum.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1964-041A|title: 10.63°S 20.6°W

sites.name: Luna 5 crash (Mare Nubium)
sites.description: First soft-landing attempt; a guidance fault stopped the braking burn and it crashed.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1965-036A|title: 8.0°N 23.0°W

sites.name: Luna 7 crash (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.description: Soft-landing attempt that crashed after its braking burn went wrong.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1965-077A|title: 9.8°N 47.8°W

sites.name: Luna 8 crash (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.description: Soft-landing attempt; a punctured airbag upset the descent and it crashed.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1965-099A|title: 9.1°N 63.3°W

sites.name: Ranger 8 impact (Mare Tranquillitatis)
sites.description: Imaged Mare Tranquillitatis, later scouted for Apollo, down to impact.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1965-010A|title: 2.638°N 24.787°E

sites.name: Ranger 9 impact (Alphonsus crater)
sites.description: Last Ranger: impact inside Alphonsus crater, broadcast live on US television.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1965-023A|title: 12.828°S 2.387°W

sites.name: Luna 9 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.description: First soft landing on the Moon and first pictures from the surface.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026): 7.08°N 64.37°W

sites.name: Surveyor 1 (Flamsteed P)
sites.description: First US soft landing, in Oceanus Procellarum.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-045A|title: 2.474°S 43.339°W

sites.name: Luna 13 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.description: Second Soviet soft landing; measured soil density with a penetrometer.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-116A|title: 18.87°N 62.05°W

sites.name: Lunar Orbiter 1 impact (far side)
sites.description: Apollo site-mapping orbiter, deliberately crashed on the far side.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-073A|title: 6.7°N 162.0°E

sites.name: Surveyor 2 crash (near Copernicus)
sites.description: A thruster failed during a course correction and the lander tumbled into the Moon.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-084A|title: 5.5°N 12.0°W

sites.name: Lunar Orbiter 2 impact (far side)
sites.description: Took the famous oblique view of Copernicus; deliberately crashed on the far side.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-100A|title: 3.0°N 119.0°E

sites.name: Lunar Orbiter 3 impact (far side)
sites.description: Photographed Surveyor 1 on the surface; deliberately crashed.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-008A|title: 14.3°N 97.7°W

sites.name: Surveyor 3 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.description: Bounced twice on landing; Apollo 12 astronauts walked over and retrieved parts of it in 1969.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-035A|title: 3.015°S 23.418°W

sites.name: Surveyor 4 crash (Sinus Medii)
sites.description: Contact was lost during the braking burn, minutes before touchdown.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-068A|title: 0.4°N 1.33°W

sites.name: Lunar Orbiter 5 impact
sites.description: Last Lunar Orbiter; mapped candidate Apollo sites and was then crashed.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-075A|title: 3.0°S 83.0°W

sites.name: Surveyor 5 (Mare Tranquillitatis)
sites.description: First chemical analysis of lunar soil, near the later Apollo 11 site.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-084A|title: 1.461°N 23.195°E

sites.name: Surveyor 6 (Sinus Medii)
sites.description: Made the first lift-off from the Moon: a hop of a few metres to a new spot.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://quickmap.lroc.im-ldi.com/?prjExtent=-43409.3499451,14353.3895196,-43156.1885415,14483.3120926&activeDrawingLayer=@@user-defined&stack=3314&selectedFeature=3005,28&isCesiumDynamicEnabled=true&shadowsType=all&proj=16&features=-1.37,0.46: 0.4743°N 1.4275°W

sites.name: Surveyor 7 (near Tycho)
sites.description: Only Surveyor in the rugged highlands, on the ejecta north of Tycho.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/534: 40.98°S 11.514°W

sites.name: Luna 16 (Mare Fecunditatis)
sites.description: First robotic sample return.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1970-072A|title: 0.68°S 56.3°E

sites.name: Luna 17 and Lunokhod 1 (Mare Imbrium)
sites.description: Delivered Lunokhod 1, the first rover on another world.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1970-095A|title: 38.28°N 35.0°W

sites.name: Luna 18 crash (Mare Fecunditatis)
sites.description: Sample-return attempt lost on descent in rough highland terrain.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1971-073A|title: 3.57°N 56.5°E

sites.name: Luna 20 (Apollonius highlands)
sites.description: Returned highland samples from between Mare Fecunditatis and Mare Crisium.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1972-007A|title: 3.57°N 56.5°E

sites.name: Luna 21 and Lunokhod 2 (Le Monnier)
sites.description: Delivered Lunokhod 2, which drove about 40 km.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1973-001A|title: 25.85°N 30.45°E

sites.name: Luna 23 (Mare Crisium)
sites.description: Damaged on landing and could not drill; Luna 24 later landed nearby.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1974-084A|title: 12.75°N 62.2°E

sites.name: Hiten impact (Furnerius)
sites.description: Japan's first lunar probe, deliberately crashed at the end of its mission.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1990-007A|title: 34.3°S 55.6°E

sites.name: Lunar Prospector impact (south polar crater)
sites.description: Crashed into a permanently shadowed crater to look for a water-vapour plume.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1998-001A|title: 87.7°S 42.35°E

sites.name: SMART-1 impact (Lacus Excellentiae)
sites.description: Europe's first lunar probe; its end-of-mission impact flash was seen from Earth.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://astronomy.com/news/2017/09/a-lunar-orbiters-final-resting-place|title=New: 34.262°S 46.193°W

sites.name: Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe (Shackleton)
sites.mission: ISRO Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe, November 2008
sites.description: India's first craft on the Moon, released to hit near Shackleton crater.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://www.unoosa.org/documents/pdf/ser570E.pdf|title=Information: 89.76°S 39.4°W

sites.name: SELENE Okina relay impact (far side)
sites.mission: JAXA SELENE (Kaguya) relay satellite Okina, February 2009
sites.description: Small relay sub-satellite that let Kaguya track the far side; its mission ended in impact.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://www.jaxa.jp/press/2009/02/20090218_sac_kaguya.pdf|title: 28.213°N 159.033°W

sites.name: Chang'e 1 impact (Mare Fecunditatis)
sites.description: China's first lunar orbiter, deliberately crashed at the end of its mission.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://ssedso.gsfc.nasa.gov/initiatives/lunar/LESWG/pubs_presentations/4thGM/bk_International_missions_lakew.ppt|title=Upcoming: 1.5°S 52.36°E

sites.description: Japan's main lunar orbiter; planned end-of-mission impact.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://www.jaxa.jp/topics/2009/06_e.html|title: 65.5°S 80.5°E

sites.name: LCROSS impact (Cabeus crater)
sites.description: Rocket stage and shepherding craft hit Cabeus; the plume confirmed water ice.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=2007-031D|title: 84.678°S 48.6926°W

sites.name: GRAIL Ebb and Flow impact (near Goldschmidt)
sites.description: Twin gravity-mapping orbiters crashed into a mountain; the site is named after Sally Ride.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news.php?release=2012-396&cid=release_2012-396|title=NASA: 75.62°N 26.63°W

sites.name: LADEE impact (far side, near Sundman V)
sites.description: Dust and exosphere orbiter; planned end-of-mission impact on the eastern rim of Sundman V crater.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026): 10.8°N 91.6°W

sites.name: Beresheet crash (Mare Serenitatis)
sites.description: First private landing attempt; an engine shut down during descent.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://www.lroc.asu.edu/posts/1101: 32.5956°N 19.3496°E

sites.name: Longjiang-2 impact (far side, Van Gent)
sites.description: Chang'e 4 relay-era microsatellite; planned impact at the end of its mission.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://www.planetary.org/blogs/guest-blogs/2019/longjiang-2-impacts-moon.html|title=Lunar: 16.6956°N 159.517°E

sites.name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram crash
sites.description: Lost guidance late in descent and crashed; its orbiter is still working.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://spacenews.com/new-details-emerge-about-failed-lunar-landings/|title=New: 70.881°S 22.784°E

sites.name: Hakuto-R Mission 1 crash (Atlas crater)
sites.description: Misjudged altitude, ran out of fuel above the surface and crashed.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC http://lroc.sese.asu.edu/posts/1302|title=Impact: 47.581°N 44.094°E

sites.name: Luna 25 crash (near Pontécoulant G)
sites.description: A faulty burn during orbit lowering sent it into the Moon before it reached its target.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://www.russianspaceweb.com/luna-glob-flight.html: 57.865°S 61.36°E

sites.name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 Resilience crash (Mare Frigoris)
sites.description: Second ispace attempt; a laser rangefinder fault led to a crash.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1456: 60.4445°N 4.588°W

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton plateau)
sites.mission: Intuitive Machines IM-2, NASA CLPS, March 2025
sites.description: Southernmost landing so far; it tipped over in a crater and stopped within a day.
sites.source: Wikipedia, 'List of artificial objects on the Moon' (Nov 2026); NSSDC https://www.lroc.asu.edu/images/1408: 84.7906°S 29.1957°E
